arxiv-1807-07915.title: Search for charged Higgs bosons decaying via H ± → τ ± ​ ν τ H^{\pm}\to\tau^{\pm}\nu_{\tau} in the τ \tau +jets and τ \tau +lepton final states with 36 fb − 1 {\mathrm{fb}^{-1}} of p ​ p pp collision data recorded at s = 13 \sqrt{s}=13 TeV with the ATLAS experiment
arxiv-1807-07915.creator: The ATLAS Collaboration
arxiv-1807-07915.description: Abstract Charged Higgs bosons produced either in top-quark decays or in association with a top-quark, subsequently decaying via H ± → τ ± ​ ν τ H^{\pm}\to\tau^{\pm}\nu_{\tau} , are searched for in 36.1 fb − 1 {\mathrm{fb}^{-1}} of proton–proton collision data at s = 13 \sqrt{s}=13 TeV recorded with the ATLAS detector.

arxiv-2101-08219.title: PRINCIPAL COMPONENT ANALYSIS FOR ESTIMATING PARAMETERS OF THE L1287 DENSE CORE BY FITTING MODEL SPECTRAL MAPS INTO OBSERVED ONES
arxiv-2101-08219.creator: L. E. Pirogov, P. M. Zemlyanukha
arxiv-2101-08219.description: Abstract An algorithm has been developed for finding the global minimum of a multidimensional error function by fitting model spectral maps into observed ones. Principal component analysis is applied to reduce the dimensionality of the model and the coupling degree between the parameters, and to determine the region of the minimum.

arxiv-2203-10013.title: PyRoboCOP : Py thon-based Robo tic C ontrol & O ptimization P ackage for Manipulation
arxiv-2203-10013.creator: Arvind U. Raghunathan, Devesh K. Jhaand Diego Romeres
arxiv-2203-10013.description: Abstract PyRoboCOP is a Python-based package for control, optimization and estimation of robotic systems described by nonlinear Differential Algebraic Equations (DAEs). In particular, the package can handle systems with contacts that are described by complementarity constraints and provides a general framework for specifying obstacle avoidance constraints.

arxiv-2401-09529.title: The Beam-Dump Ceiling and Its Experimental Implication: The Case of a Portable Experiment
arxiv-2401-09529.creator: Doojin Kim, Jaehoon Yu, Jong-Chul Park, Hyunyong Kim
arxiv-2401-09529.description: Abstract We generalize the nature of the so-called beam-dump “ceiling” beyond which the improvement on the sensitivity reach in the search for fast-decaying mediators dramatically slows down, and point out its experimental implications that motivate tabletop-size beam-dump experiments for the search.

arxiv-2406-15884.title: LMod R ​ ( \V ) \mathrm{LMod}_{R}(\V) -enriched ∞ \infty -categories are left R R -module objects of \Cat \V \Cat^{\V} and \Cat \V \Cat^{\V} -enriched ∞ \infty -functors
arxiv-2406-15884.creator: Matteo Doni
arxiv-2406-15884.description: Abstract We establish the feasibility of investigating the theory of LMod R ​ ( \V ) \mathrm{LMod}_{R}(\V) -enriched ∞ \infty -categories, where R R is an 𝔼 1 \mathbb{E}_{1} -ring of a presentable 𝔼 2 \mathbb{E}_{2} -monoidal ∞ \infty -category 𝒱 \mathcal{V} , through the framework of \V \V -enriched ∞ \infty -category theory.

arxiv-2407-07451.title: Hopf algebra structures for the backward error analysis of ergodic stochastic differential equations
arxiv-2407-07451.creator: Eugen Bronasco, Adrien Laurent
arxiv-2407-07451.description: Abstract While backward error analysis does not generalise straightforwardly to the strong and weak approximation of stochastic differential equations, it extends for the sampling of ergodic dynamics. The calculation of the modified equation relies on tedious calculations and there is no expression of the modified vector field, in opposition to the deterministic setting.

arxiv-2501-08134.title: An Empirical Wall-Pressure Spectrum Model for Aeroacoustic Predictions Based on Symbolic Regression
arxiv-2501-08134.creator: Botero-Bolívar, Laura, Huergo, David, dos Santos, Fernanda L, Venner, Cornelis H, de Santana, Leandro D, Ferrer, Esteban
arxiv-2501-08134.description: Abstract Fast-turn around methods to predict airfoil trailing-edge noise are crucial for incorporating noise limitations into design optimization loops of several applications. Among these aeroacoustic predictive models, Amiet’s theory offers the best balance between accuracy and simplicity. The accuracy of the model relies heavily on precise wall-pressure spectrum predictions, which are often based on single-equation formulations with adjustable parameters.

arxiv-2504-01688.title: Enhancing European Cooperation in the Search for Dark Matter
arxiv-2504-01688.creator: Bernard Andrieu, Ties Behnke, Philip Bechtle, Xavier Bertou, Jose Busto, Susana Cebrián, Marco Cirelli, Laurent Derome, Cristinel Diaconu, Caterina Doglioni, Guiliana Fiorillo, Davide Franco, Juan Fuster, Romain Gaior, Erika Garutti, Claudio Gatti, B. Gimeno-Martinez, Frédéric Girard, Roxanne Guenet
arxiv-2504-01688.description: Abstract The search for dark matter is an exciting topic that is pursued in different communities over a wide range of masses and using a variety of experimental approaches. The result is a strongly correlated matrix of activities across Europe and beyond, both on the experimental and the theoretical side.

arxiv-2507-10960.title: Whom to Respond To? A Transformer-Based Model for Multi-Party Social Robot Interaction
arxiv-2507-10960.creator: He Zhu, Ryo Miyoshi, Yuki Okafuji
arxiv-2507-10960.description: Abstract Prior human-robot interaction (HRI) research has primarily focused on single-user interactions, where robots do not need to consider the timing or recipient of their responses. However, in multi-party interactions, such as at malls and hospitals, social robots must understand the context and decide both when and to whom they should respond.

arxiv-2509-10852.title: Pre-Storage Reasoning for Episodic Memory: Shifting Inference Burden to Memory for Personalized Dialogue
arxiv-2509-10852.creator: Sangyeop Kim, Yohan Lee, Sanghwa Kim, Hyunjong Kim, Sungzoon Cho
arxiv-2509-10852.description: Abstract Effective long-term memory in conversational AI requires synthesizing information across multiple sessions. However, current systems place excessive reasoning burden on response generation, making performance significantly dependent on model sizes. We introduce PREMem (Pre-storage Reasoning for Episodic Memory), a novel approach that shifts complex reasoning processes from inference to memory construction.

arxiv-2512-10979.title: Seamless Transitions: A Comprehensive Review of Live Migration Technologies
arxiv-2512-10979.creator: Sima Attar-Khorasani, Lincoln Sherpa, Matthias Lieber, Siavash Ghiasvand
arxiv-2512-10979.description: Abstract Live migration, a technology enabling seamless transition of operational computational entities between various hosts while preserving continuous functionality and client connectivity, has been the subject of extensive research. However, existing reviews often overlook critical technical aspects and practical challenges integral to the usage of live migration techniques in real-world scenarios.

arxiv-2602-15125.title: GKP-inspired high-dimensional superdense coding with energy-time entanglement
arxiv-2602-15125.creator: Kai-Chi Chang, Arjun Mirani, Murat Can Sarihan, Xiang Cheng, Michelle Harasimowicz, Patrick Hayden, and Chee Wei Wong
arxiv-2602-15125.description: Abstract Superdense coding, the application of entanglement to boost classical communication capacity, is a cornerstone of quantum communication. In this paper, we propose a high-dimensional superdense coding protocol using energy-time entangled states. These states are biphoton frequency combs, an example of entangled time-frequency Gottesman-Kitaev-Preskill (TFGKP) states or time-frequency grid states.

arxiv-2602-23322.title: The metric fundamental class of non-orientable manifolds and manifolds with boundary Thanks: D.M. was supported by Swiss National Science Foundation grant 212867.
arxiv-2602-23322.creator: Denis Marti
arxiv-2602-23322.description: Abstract . We introduce the metric fundamental class for metric spaces that are homeomorphic to compact, non-orientable, smooth manifolds with (possibly empty) boundary. This is an integer rectifiable current that provides an analytic representation of the topological fundamental class of the space.

britannica-1911-massif.title: Massif (1911 Encyclopaedia Britannica article)
britannica-1911-massif.creator: Encyclopaedia Britannica
britannica-1911-massif.description: Article 'Massif' from the 1911 Encyclopædia Britannica (Volume 17), the classic English-language general encyclopedia, now in the public domain. geography for a mountainous mass or group of connected heights, whether isolated or forming part of a larger mountain system. A “massif” is more or less clearly marked off by valleys.

doe-osti-3375831-collaborative-research-.creator: Wurtele, Jonathan S.
doe-osti-3375831-collaborative-research-.description: U.S. Department of Energy technical report. This award supported Berkeley contributions to the ALPHA antihydrogen program from the years 2018–2025, emphasizing nonneutral-plasma control, plasma-based magnetic-field diagnostics, patch-field measurements, antihydrogen trap dynamics, and experimental protocols and statistical

pmc-11300178.title: Accuracy of MRI Versus PET/CT in the Prediction of Treatment Response to Neoadjuvant Chemotherapy in Breast Cancer
pmc-11300178.creator: Noof Alshaibani, Janaki Krithika Chandramohan, Yusuf Althawadi, Maryam Almusalam, Sara S Khairi, Hamad S Saif, Khalid Al Sindi, Salwa Aly
pmc-11300178.description: BackgroundBreast-conserving surgeries have significantly advanced breast cancer treatment, offering favorable oncological outcomes, enhanced cosmetic results, reduced postoperative morbidity, and better psychological acceptance compared to mastectomy. The introduction of neoadjuvant therapy has expanded the applicability of breast conservation surgery to include locally advanced tumors.

pmc-11518102.title: Co-creation of migrant health interventions in Portugal: Insights from the VO(I)CES project
pmc-11518102.creator: M J Marques, A Seyfulayeva, S Hamwi, A S Machado, A Gama, R Osbourne, S Dias
pmc-11518102.description: BackgroundInternational migration is increasing both globally and in Europe, highlighting the need for responsive interventions that cater to the diverse needs and strengths of migrants. Although genuine involvement of stakeholders in the design and implementation of interventions is vital to enhance their relevance, responsiveness, and ownership, co-created migrant health interventions remain limited.

pmc-12403546.title: The ‘selves’ in doping and its psychosocial mechanisms: harmonised multi-country evidence from high-performing athletes in the UK, US, and China
pmc-12403546.creator: Shuge Zhang, Ian Boardley, Jingdong Liu, Jules Woolf
pmc-12403546.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). BackgroundDoping remains an ongoing threat to clean competition. To date, global preventive initiatives have not addressed critical psychosocial antecedents of doping thoroughly due to the scarcity of knowledge regarding its psychosocial mechanisms from a harmonised cross-country perspective.

pmc-12785804.title: Triterpenoids CDDO and CDDO-EA Inhibit the Replication of Hepatitis B Virus by Modulating Nucleocapsid Assembly
pmc-12785804.creator: Qiang Gao, Ge Yang, Ya Wang, Lu Yang, Jin Hu, Huiqiang Wang, Haiyan Yan, Kun Wang, Shuo Wu, Yuhuan Li, Jiandong Jiang
pmc-12785804.description: Chronic hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection remains a global public health challenge, and the currently approved medications can not achieve a cure. Synthetic triterpenoids have shown promising therapeutic potential for liver pathologies. In our search for novel antiviral agents against HBV, we found that two triterpenoids, 2-cyano-3,12-dioxooleana-1,9-dien-28-oic acid (CDDO) and CDDO-ethyl amide (CDDO-EA), significantly inhibited HBV DNA replication.

pmc-12841074.title: REV1 Loss Triggers a G2/M Cell-Cycle Arrest Through Dysregulation of Mitotic Regulators
pmc-12841074.creator: Brailey Buntin, Madison Guyette, Vihit Gupta, Kanayo Ikeh, Sombodhi Bhattacharya, Erica N. Lamkin, Allison Lafuze, Roxana del Rio-Guerra, Jiyong Hong, Pei Zhou, Nimrat Chatterjee
pmc-12841074.description: Background: Genomic integrity is crucial to the cellular life cycle, which involves a tightly regulated process where cells progress through specific phases to ensure that fully replicated, undamaged DNA is inherited by daughter cells. Any dysfunction in this process or unrepaired DNA damage leads to cell cycle arrest and programmed cell death.

pmc-13059175.title: A novel blood collection technique from the rat thoracic aorta: employing a diaphragm sac as a reservoir
pmc-13059175.creator: Purvaj G. Barote, Abdulla Sherikar, Sameer N. Goyal, Sanjay N. Awathale
pmc-13059175.description: BackgroundSeveral blood withdrawal techniques are employed for biochemical research. However, these techniques fail to fulfil the desired requirement of blood volume. We invented the alternative method of blood collection through the thoracic aorta in an anesthetized rat. Under anesthesia, the rat was placed supine, and a transverse abdominal incision was made.

pmc-13478637.title: Bacteriophage-mediated restoration of epithelial integrity, DNA damage response, and transcriptomic homeostasis in colon organoids exposed to ETBF and pks + E. coli
pmc-13478637.creator: Myoung Hyoun Song, Eun Kyoung Oh, In Hwang Kim, Jee-Soo Son, Seong Jun Yoon, Jin-Young Kim, Min Jung Kim, Seung-Yong Jeong, Ji Won Park, Ja-Lok Ku
pmc-13478637.description: Colorectal cancer (CRC)–associated pathobionts such as Enterotoxigenic Bacteroides fragilis (ETBF) and colibactin-producing (pks+) Escherichia coli disrupt epithelial barrier function, promote chronic inflammation, and induce genotoxic stress. To investigate how these pathogenic interactions with the host epithelium can be modulated, we employed patient-derived normal human colon organoids as an ex vivo model.
